passage: The supermarket in Nairobi was busy. Wanjiru said no to the sweets. Kamau, two, dropped to the floor. He screamed. He kicked his legs and arched his back. He threw his shoe. Wanjiru knelt. "Kamau, listen, please..." He screamed louder. People turned to look. Her friend Mina, pushing the trolley, whispered, "He can't hear anything right now." Wanjiru nodded and stayed close, waiting.

qa.q: What did Kamau throw?
qa.a: He threw his shoe.

qa.q: Why could Kamau not listen to his mother?
qa.a: He was too upset to listen or reason, because a toddler's brain cannot calm itself down yet.

qa.q: What choice did Wanjiru make that helped?
qa.a: She stopped trying to talk him out of it and stayed close, waiting for the storm to pass.

qa.q: How might Wanjiru feel with people turning to look?
qa.a: She may feel embarrassed and stressed, but Mina's words help her stay calm.

grounding: It shows a toddler at the peak of a tantrum, dropping, screaming, kicking, throwing and arching, unable to listen or reason.

passage: I'm Manjula, from the flat downstairs. Yesterday in the lobby I saw Devika's little boy, Kanha, lying on the floor. He was screaming and kicking. He threw his toy car at the wall. Devika was saying, "Kanha, stop, listen to Mumma." He only screamed more and arched his back. I don't think he could hear her at all. Devika moved the toy car away and sat near him.

qa.q: What did Kanha throw at the wall?
qa.a: He threw his toy car at the wall.

qa.q: Why does Manjula think Kanha could not hear his mother?
qa.a: He was in the middle of a big storm of feeling, screaming more and arching his back, too upset to listen.

qa.q: What did Devika do that was helpful?
qa.a: She moved the toy car away to keep things safe and sat near Kanha instead of arguing with him.

qa.q: How does the scene look to Manjula?
qa.a: Manjula sees a toddler overwhelmed by feelings and a mother trying hard to cope.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler at the height of a tantrum, screaming, kicking and throwing, unable to listen or reason.

passage:
"Kamal, no more biscuits. Dinner soon."

"Biscuit!"

"No, beta."

Kamal dropped to the floor. He screamed, kicking his legs against the tiles.

"Kamal—"

He threw his toy car. It hit the door.

"Kamal, listen—"

He arched his back and screamed louder, eyes squeezed shut.

"Okay," said Akash softly, sitting down on the floor nearby. "Okay."

He moved the other toy cars out of reach and waited.

qa.q: What did Kamal throw?
qa.a: His toy car.

qa.q: Why can't Kamal listen when Akash says "Kamal, listen"?
qa.a: He is in a storm of anger and frustration, and at his age he cannot yet calm himself enough to listen.

qa.q: Which choice did Akash make that helps?
qa.a: He stopped trying to reason, sat nearby quietly, moved the cars out of reach, and waited.

qa.q: How might Akash be feeling as he sits on the floor?
qa.a: He is probably tired and a little stressed, but choosing to stay calm.

grounding: Toddler Kamal drops to the floor, screams, kicks, throws and arches his back, unable to listen, while Akash stays calm nearby.

passage:
Daycare note, Friday

At snack time Nilesh (2) wanted the red cup, which another child had. When I offered the blue cup, he dropped to the floor, screamed and kicked his feet. He threw the blue cup and arched his back when I tried to lift him.

He could not hear anything I said. I moved the chairs away, sat beside him and waited. After a few minutes the screaming slowed.

I will tell his mother at pick-up.

— Ganga

qa.q: Which cup did Nilesh want?
qa.a: The red cup.

qa.q: Why couldn't Nilesh hear Ganga?
qa.a: He was overwhelmed by anger, and at two he cannot yet calm himself or listen during a storm.

qa.q: What did Ganga do well?
qa.a: Ganga moved the chairs for safety, sat beside Nilesh without arguing, and waited until he slowed down.

qa.q: How might the other child with the red cup feel?
qa.a: They may feel startled or confused by the screaming.

grounding: A daycare note shows two-year-old Nilesh at the peak of a tantrum, screaming, kicking, throwing and arching, unable to listen.

At the weekly haat in their village, Ojas wanted the plastic whistle hanging at the toy stall. Suraj said no.

Ojas threw himself down on the dusty ground. He screamed and kicked, knocking over a basket of onions. When Suraj reached for him, he arched his back and hit out.

People stared. The onion seller frowned.

Suraj didn't argue. He moved the basket away, crouched beside Ojas, and waited.

qa.q: What did Ojas want from the toy stall?
qa.a: The plastic whistle.

qa.q: Why did Ojas hit out when Suraj reached for him?
qa.a: He was overwhelmed by anger and frustration, and his brain cannot yet calm itself or listen at this age.

qa.q: What did Suraj do that helped?
qa.a: He didn't argue; he moved the basket away for safety, crouched beside Ojas and waited.

qa.q: How might the onion seller feel?
qa.a: The onion seller seems annoyed, frowning at the mess.

grounding: At a village haat, toddler Ojas drops, screams, kicks and arches his back, unable to listen, while his father keeps him safe and waits.

passage: In a busy Madrid supermarket, Mateo, almost three, dropped flat onto the cold floor by the fruit. He screamed, kicked his shoes off and arched his back like a bridge. His dad, Sami, crouched down. "Mateo, listen, we'll..." Mateo threw a mandarin, then another. He couldn't hear a word. His cheeks were scarlet and his breath came in gulps. Sami moved the bag of apples out of reach and waited.

qa.q: What did Mateo throw?
qa.a: He threw a mandarin, then another.

qa.q: What does Mateo's arching and screaming suggest about what he is feeling?
qa.a: He is overwhelmed by a huge, angry storm of feeling, far too upset to hear or reason.

qa.q: What is the most useful thing Sami can do during the peak?
qa.a: Stay close and calm, keep Mateo safe by moving things out of reach, and wait instead of trying to reason.

qa.q: What might Sami be feeling in the middle of the busy supermarket?
qa.a: Sami may feel embarrassed and stressed with people around, yet he chooses to stay calm and wait.

grounding: Shows a toddler at the peak of a tantrum, screaming, kicking, throwing and arching, unable to listen or reason.
